title: Fixing the District of Columbia Act of 2025

sections.heading: SHORT TITLE.
sections.text: This act may be cited as “Fixing the District of Columbia Act of 2025” or “FDCA”.

sections.heading: PURPOSE.
sections.text: The purpose of this Act is to fix the District of Columbia by shutting down its municipal government, transferring municipal departments to federal departments, and reestablish the Delegate of the District of Columbia after a long history of shortcomings by the municipality.

sections.heading: FINDINGS.
sections.text:
Congress finds the following:
(a) Over the past six (6) months, the District of Columbia Municipal Government, not including its municipal departments, has been allotted over $500,000.00; (b)During those six (6) months, the District of Columbia City Council has proposed less than six (6) pieces of legislation; (c) During those six (6) months, the District of Columbia Municipal Government has failed to employ an Inspector General as required by Title VII of the District of Columbia Code; (d)The Metropolitan Police Department and the District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services have operated without sufficient oversight by the District of Columbia Municipal Government; and (e) The District of Columbia Municipal Government has overall lacked sufficient performance.

sections.heading: REPEALMENTS.
sections.text: (a) REPEALED LAWS.—Upon enactment, the following laws shall be repealed in their entirety: (i) Pub. L. 16-120 (The Hail Columbia Act) (ii) Pub. L. 25-181 (Federal District of Columbia Criminal Code) (iii) Pub. L. 29-213 (D.C Delegate Elimination Act) (iv) Pub. L. 29-216 (District of Columbia Home Rule Act of 2025) (v) Pub. L. 30-223 (Municipal Transportation Act) (vi) Pub. L. 32-231 (District Improvement Act)

sections.heading: DEFINITIONS.
sections.text:
For the purposes of this act: (a) MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT.—The term “municipal government” means the municipal government that was established under Pub. L. 29-216 (District of Columbia Home Rule Act). (b)METROPOLITAN POLICE DEPARTMENT.—The term “Metropolitan Police Department” or “MPD” means the Metropolitan Police Department of the District of Columbia.
(c) DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA FIRE AND EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES.—The term “District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services” or “DCFEMS” means the Fire and Emergency Medical Services of the District of Columbia. (d)SECRETARY.—The term “secretary” means the head of the Department of Homeland Security, known as the Secretary of Homeland Security. (e) ATTORNEY GENERAL.—The term “attorney general” means the head of the Department of Justice, known as the Attorney General of the United States. (f) TRANSITION PERIOD.—The term “transition period” means the 14-day period following the enactment of this Act during which federal transfer and restructuring shall take place.

sections.heading: DISSOLUTION OF THE MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT.
sections.text: (a) DISSOLUTION.—The municipal government of the District of Columbia, established under the District of Columbia Home Rule Act of 2025, is hereby dissolved effective seven (7) days after enactment of this Act. (b)REPEALMENT OF MUNICIPAL LAWS.—Any District law, ordinance, or regulation inconsistent with this Act shall be repealed unless otherwise specified in this Act. (c) CONGRESSIONAL CONTROL.—The District shall remain under direct congressional control pursuant to Article I, Section VIII, Clause 16 of the United States Constitution.

sections.heading: TRANSFER OF THE METROPOLITAN POLICE DEPARTMENT TO THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE.
sections.text:
(a) TRANSFER.—The Metropolitan Police Department is hereby transferred to the Department of Justice as a federal component. (b)ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROL.—The Attorney General, and/or an individual delegated the same authority by the Attorney General, shall exercise all powers of direction, control, and supervision over the Metropolitan Police Department. (c) EMPLOYMENT STATUS.—All sworn officers and civilian employees of the Metropolitan Police Department shall become federal employees under the Department of Justice, retaining their pay, benefits, and position during the transition period.
(d)MISSION.—The Metropolitan Police Department shall serve as a federal law enforcement agency within the District of Columbia to protect and serve all life and property. (e) LEADERSHIP.—The Chief and Deputy Chief of the Metropolitan Police Department shall be appointed by the Attorney General. (f) OVERSIGHT.—The Inspector General of the Department of Justice shall have the same authority over the Metropolitan Police Department as any other component within the Department of Justice. (g)REGULATIONS.—The Attorney General shall establish regulations to implement this section no later than seven (7) days after enactment of this Act.

sections.heading: TRANSFER OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA FIRE AND EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES TO THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY.
sections.text:
(a) TRANSFER.—The District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services is hereby transferred to the Department of Homeland Security as a federal component. (b)ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROL.— (i) The Secretary, and/or an individual delegated the same authority as the Secretary, shall exercise all powers of direction, control, and supervision over the District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services. (c) EMPLOYMENT STATUS.—All sworn firefighters and civilian employees of the District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services shall become federal employees under the Department of Homeland Security, retaining their pay, benefits, and position during the transition period. (d)MISSION.—The District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services shall serve as a federal public safety agency within the District of Columbia to serve and protect all life and property. (e) LEADERSHIP.—The Chief and Deputy Chief of the District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services shall be appointed by the Secretary. (f) OVERSIGHT.—The Inspector General of the Department of Homeland Security shall have the same authority over the District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services as any other component within the Department of Homeland Security.
(g)REGULATIONS.—The Secretary shall establish regulations to implement this section no later than seven (7) days after enactment of this Act.

sections.heading: REESTABLISHING THE DELEGATE OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA.
sections.text: (a) REESTABLISHMENT.— The Delegate of the District of Columbia to the House of Representatives is hereby reestablished. (b)VOTING POWER.—The Delegate of the District of Columbia shall have no voting power within the floor of the House of Representatives but may sit on, cast votes in, and chair congressional committees. (c) LEGISLATIVE POWER.—The Delegate of the District of Columbia shall hold the authority to propose legislation, bills, resolutions, joint resolutions, concurrent resolutions, amendments, and other formal documentation to the House of Representatives. (d)ELECTION.—The Delegate of the District of Columbia shall be elected separately from the House of Representatives in an independent partisan election held by the Federal Election Commission and shall be elected by qualified electors of the district, for a term specified in Article I, Section II, Clause 1 of the Constitution. (i) Upon enactment of this bill the Delegate of the District of Columbia shall be placed upon the official ballot for any and all upcoming elections concurrent to the House of Representatives. (e) REPRESENTATION.—The Delegate of the District of Columbia shall solely represent the District of Columbia's At-Large Congressional District. (f) DESIGNATION.—This office shall be designated as an official public office pursuant to this Act.

sections.heading: ADOPTION OF MUNICIPAL LAWS INTO FEDERAL LAWS.
sections.text:
(a) DISTRICT TORT ACT.—The ‘District Tort Act,’ as proposed to the Council of the District of Columbia on April 4, 2025, is hereby adopted and enacted as federal law under this Act with the following amendment:
(i) Section 4(c) shall be amended to read: “The term "special prosecutor" means an attorney assigned to the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia.” (b)THE DC CRIMINAL CODE.—‘The DC Criminal Code,’ as proposed to the Council of the District of Columbia on April 24, 2025, is hereby adopted and enacted as federal law under this Act with the following amendment: (i) Subsection 11 shall be created under Section 102 and read: “Pursuant to this code, the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia shall have the sole responsibility for prosecuting any offences under this code and may be referred to as a ‘special prosecutor.’” (c) PROTECTING OUR FIREFIGHTERS ACT.—The ‘Protecting our Firefighters Act,’ as proposed to the Council of the District of Columbia on July 6, 2025, is hereby adopted and enacted as federal law under this Act. (d)FIRE MARSHALS ACT.—The ‘Fire Marshals Act,’ as proposed to the Council of the District of Columbia on August 22, 2025, is hereby adopted and enacted as federal law under this Act with the following amendment: (i) Section 4(1)(c)(iii) shall be amended to read: “The Chief Fire Marshal shall give a monthly report of all properties inspected and all violations found in those properties to the Chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, Chief of the District of Columbia Fire Department, and the Secretary of Homeland Security.” (e) SAFEGUARD CLAUSE.—All adopted municipal laws under this Section shall remain in force until amended or repealed by Congress.

sections.heading: AMENDMENT TO THE LLEARN ACT.
sections.text:
(a) AMENDMENTS.—Upon enactment, the following amendments shall be applied to Pub. L. 22-156 (Local Law Enforcement Agencies Reform and Nurturing): (i) Section 6(1)(1) shall be amended to read: “It is hereby established the Metropolitan Police Department as a law enforcement component within the Department of Justice under the authority and direction of the Attorney General of the United States, which shall act as the primary law enforcement agency within the District of Columbia.”
(ii) Section 6(2)(1) shall be amended to read: “The principal head of the Metropolitan Police Department shall be the Chief of Police, who shall be appointed by the Attorney General of the United States, and who shall serve at the pleasure of the President.” (iii) Section 6(2)(2) shall be amended to read: “There is established in the Metropolitan Police Department the office of Deputy Chief of Police of the Metropolitan Police Department, who shall be appointed by the Attorney General of the United States, and who shall serve at the pleasure of the President. The Deputy Chief of Police shall perform such duties as may be prescribed by the Chief of Police or required by law. The Deputy Chief shall: a. in case of the death, resignation, or removal from office of the Chief, perform the duties of the Chief until a successor is appointed; and b. in case of the absence or sickness of the Chief, perform the duties of the Chief until such absence or sickness shall terminate.”

sections.heading: SEVERABILITY.
sections.text: This Act shall be severable, such that if any word, phrase, line, sentence, or provision of this Act, or the application of any of them to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, their application to other persons or circumstances, and the remainder of this Act shall not be affected thereby. This act shall not be superseded by any newer law unless that law specifically declares its intent to supersede this Act’s provisions.

sections.heading: ENACTMENT.
sections.text: This Act shall take effect immediately after enactment.
